subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw scope/reset persisted update offsets by apiRoot and tolerate only the migration-specific 400 Logged out deleteWebhook response?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the permanent behavior changes persisted polling state and startup failure policy, which are compatibility-sensitive maintainer decisions under the repo guidance.

options.title: Endpoint-aware state plus narrow tolerance
options.body: Add apiRoot identity or endpoint-switch reset handling for offsets, tolerate only the expected migration Logged out response, and require focused tests plus live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor/manual reset only
options.body: Keep runtime offset identity unchanged and document or doctor-fix the local Bot API switch by clearing the Telegram offset state explicitly.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Do not choose the policy until a maintainer or reporter reproduces the full raw-update-to-dispatch failure on a live local Bot API server.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware state plus narrow tolerance
recommendation.body: Add apiRoot identity or endpoint-switch reset handling for offsets, tolerate only the expected migration Logged out response, and require focused tests plus live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram polling and Bot API error-classification work makes this the best available owner for the startup/error policy side, with state owners available for the offset part.
